feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/operations expertise. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it would be stronger with tighter formatting, fewer overlapping skills sections, and more outcome-focused metrics.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, culminating in director-level leadership; this supports credibility and seniority well.  
- Strong domain fit: digital strategy, Drupal/CMS modernization, analytics, multimedia, and advocacy/public-sector communications are consistently reinforced.  
- Writing is polished and professional, with no obvious misspellings; tone is consistent and responsibilities are easy to understand.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable impact beyond scope metrics: include outcomes such as engagement growth, email performance, traffic improvements, cost savings, adoption rates, or efficiency gains.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidating these would improve structure and make the CV feel sharper.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; standardize serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs later lists without the final comma); and consider replacing “A2/Learning” with “A2 (learning)” for cleaner style.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding a sharper leadership/value angle would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, standard CV phrasing.
- Lead with your current market value: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Reduce the channel list slightly; the detailed skills sections already cover web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving web, content, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations, with a strong track record of building scalable workflows, governance, and systems. Experienced in advocacy messaging, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, audience-focused content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” are repeated in Core Competencies/Topline Skills.
- The long channel list overlaps with both Work Experience and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value, more distinctive capabilities will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “CMS modernization,” “Editorial governance,” “Analytics & insight reporting.”
- Reduce overlap with soft-skill phrasing like “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination”; make it more outcome-oriented or remove it.
- Consider a tighter rewrite: Enterprise digital strategy • CMS modernization & web operations • Editorial workflows & governance • Cross-channel communications • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow architecture & automation • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Standardize style: use either “and” or “&” consistently; “Multi-channel” is fine, but “cross-channel” may align better with the rest of the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital strategy,” “multi-channel communications,” and “policy/advocacy communication” are already stated in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and reads less like a core competency than the other items.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic/technical breadth, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the footer projects and prior NACo entries. Tighten around scope, outcomes, and the most senior differentiators.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + client type + remit: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant to a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, web modernization, and content operations.”
- Consolidate bullets into 4–5 impact-led lines; start with verbs like “Led,” “Built,” “Developed,” “Advised,” “Launched.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: size of web estate, number of stakeholders/publishers, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search/discovery improvements, workflow time saved, or engagement gains.
- Emphasize what is new vs prior NACo roles: AI-enabled search, Drupal microsite architecture, enterprise governance, and cross-channel operating model.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite/storytelling work duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level and let the footer hold examples.
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, web improvement” echoes the 2022–2024 NACo role; distinguish by consulting scope and current transformation initiatives.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. Tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad opener with a sharper scope statement: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the flagship achievement and outcome: “Spearheaded redesign and Drupal migration of a 10,000+ page website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add growth, engagement, production volume, or campaign impact for email/social if available; otherwise shorten.
- Combine infrastructure/governance bullets for concision: “Built analytics and publishing systems across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, strengthening reporting, governance, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version higher-level and more strategic.
- Video production/studio language may duplicate older NACo roles and Recent Projects; emphasize building institutional capacity, not routine production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to execution-level leadership and channel growth, with tighter phrasing and clearer outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Built cross-team editorial planning processes linking communications, advocacy and program staff.
- Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency, speed and coordination.
- If possible, add metrics: email open/click rates, video cadence/views, publishing volume, or workflow time saved.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is too close to the Director role’s opening line.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent roles. It should be tighter and more distinctive, emphasizing leadership scope rather than repeating generic communications terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector digital engagement
- Audience and messaging strategy
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Mission-driven stakeholder communications” if targeting broader roles beyond advocacy.
- Keep each line noun-based and parallel; avoid “focused”/“planning” filler.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable outcomes for experience bullets rather than skills lists.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems/governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear in the header and Core Competencies.
- “Audience-focused content planning” overlaps with editorial coordination and storytelling already shown in NACo roles and recent projects.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it’s too long and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills item, make it more strategic and grouped around recent, high-value capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Prioritize the most current/recently evidenced strengths: Drupal, CMS modernization, API/workflow automation, AI-enabled search.
- Remove lower-priority platforms unless central to target roles; “WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages” can dilute the stronger enterprise web narrative.
- Use consistent parallel structure and fewer items to improve scanability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and let the technical section hold the full platform list.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies and the header summary; avoid repeating it verbatim in too many places.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory rather than a leadership-level skills line. It should better reflect strategic analytics ownership and avoid repeating the Technical + IT section.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting.”
- Group tools more tightly: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger business language like “executive dashboards” or “decision-support reporting.”
- Consider: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive dashboards and decision-support reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO and performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave full tool inventory to Technical + IT.
- “SEO and performance analysis” overlaps with broader analytics language; “performance optimization” is cleaner and less repetitive.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it’s too generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize operational scope and production leadership rather than listing basic capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task-level skills to higher-value delivery language: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ and multi-camera studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to better match the NACo studio build and leadership-level experience.
- Shorten “Hybrid and virtual event production” to “Hybrid and virtual event delivery” for stronger execution language.
- If space allows, add one differentiator tied to recent work: “Recurring advocacy programming” or “In-house studio operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Tool-level detail like PTZ/studio workflows is also partly covered in Technical + IT, so keep this section outcome-focused.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section almost exactly. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/current platforms or differentiated by proficiency/context.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize most relevant/current tools first: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light context instead of a bare list: **Drupal (migration, microsites, governance) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** if it’s minor compared with enterprise CMS work; it weakens the seniority signal.
- If you want stronger positioning, rename the item to **CMS & Web Platforms** and keep the list tightly aligned to recent experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is highly redundant with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep one list shorter or use one section for platforms and the other for broader capabilities.
- Drupal already appears repeatedly in recent roles/projects, so avoid over-indexing on it elsewhere unless adding new context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation-level tools that support recent Drupal, AI search, and workflow work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/refocus to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Drop **jQuery** unless it is still actively used in current/freelance work; it can date the profile and adds little if JavaScript is already listed.
- Consider grouping by function for clarity: **Front-end:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript | **Integrations & deployment:** API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions | **Tagging:** Google Tag Manager
- If space allows elsewhere, add one proof point instead of more tools, e.g. “Used for Drupal microsites, AI-enabled search implementation, and workflow automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” is covered elsewhere; avoid implying GitHub Actions duplicates that broader automation section.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as an undifferentiated software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere. Make it more selective and grouped around actual operating strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Group by function for faster scanning: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Team collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- Prioritize the strongest/recent tools first; if Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier are the real hands-on systems, keep those prominent and consider dropping one weaker PM tool.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to impact: **workflow automation, intake systems, cross-team coordination**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” already appears under Topline Skills; avoid repeating Airtable as a headline strength in both places unless this section is purely a tool inventory.
- “Workflow automation” is already named in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, so this item should stay tool-specific rather than restating the concept.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this line should stay concise and tool-focused rather than restating channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform naming for readability and ATS matching: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add one functional qualifier instead of more tools: **email automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Keep only platforms you used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was light/older exposure, consider removing it to sharpen credibility

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding claims like “managed newsletters” or “email campaigns” here; those are already covered in Work Experience.
- If Higher Logic or Mailchimp were not central in the 2022–2024 role, this item may overstate recency compared with stronger current systems experience.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Emphasize “firsts,” scope, and concrete outputs so it reads as the foundation for later leadership rather than a repeat of it.

Suggested edit:
- Open with progression + team-building: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Make contributions more concrete: specify the website refresh scope, cadence of weekly video updates, number/type of livestreams, or channels supported if known.
- Tighten phrasing and foreground outcomes: “improved workflows across web, email, social, and video” is stronger than “strengthening workflows.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving workflows across web, email, social, and video. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; differentiate here as launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating broad channel ownership already covered more strongly in the 2018–2024 roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the strongest differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast…”
- Replace generic phrasing like “coordinated innovation and research projects” with clearer scope and support level.
- Split into 2 concise bullets, e.g.:
- Supported county innovation and policy initiatives by coordinating research projects, synthesizing findings, and developing materials for organizational programs.
- Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production; also produced digital and multimedia content supporting program and policy communications.
- Add any measurable detail if available: number of episodes, audience growth, stakeholders supported, or projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on podcast launch and research/program support.
- Avoid overstating leadership here since stronger management ownership appears in 2015–2024 roles.
